author: David Reed
summary: chg-33 corrects GC-034 from DENIED to PRE_FLIGHT_ESCALATE per David's call -- the second case (after chg-31's GC-036) found asserting an outcome a pre-flight safety boundary forbids. The outcome is right on the merits, but the mechanism producing it is not: branch 4 fires here through three separate keyword defects, so the expectation is explicitly coupled to bugs that remain open, and a test pins that coupling.

changes.description: Correct GC-034's expected_outcome to PRE_FLIGHT_ESCALATE / BRANCH_4_EXPERIMENTAL, re-point reasoning_must_include at the machine-generated pre-flight rationale, and rewrite judge_scoring_criteria which previously penalised the now-correct outcome. Add a coupling test pinning that branch 4 currently fires on this case only through three defective keyword hits.
changes.failure_pattern: A second golden case asserted an outcome the architecture forbids. GC-034 expected DENIED while its own clinical_notes trip the experimental-treatment pre-flight, so the DecisionAgent is never called and the expectation could never be met. Its permanent failure had been read as an agent defect, exactly as GC-036's was.
changes.root_cause: The dataset and the pre-flight tree disagree about who decides. GC-034's author reasoned from the coverage merits -- no compendia listing, therefore not covered, therefore DENIED -- without accounting for branch 4 firing first. CLAUDE.md is explicit that the escalation tree overrides; a case cannot opt out by asserting a different outcome. Compounding it, judge_scoring_criteria said 'Penalize for auto-approval or IN_REVIEW', so even a correct escalation would have scored badly.
predicted_fixes: GC-034 becomes satisfiable: the escalation it triggers is now the expected outcome, and branch-4 coverage rises from 2 cases (GC-006, GC-009) to 3.
Its constraints stop asserting on text that cannot appear. must_include targets the pre-flight rationale rather than agent prose the agent is never invoked to write.
The judge stops penalising the correct answer.
The coupling to branch 4's defects is made loud rather than implicit: repairing branch 4 turns the new test red with a message saying GC-034's expectation must be re-decided.
risk_cases: The expectation rests on three open defects, and that is stated rather than hidden. Branch 4 fires here via substring matching (one 'No published Phase III data' -> phase i + ii + iii), no negation awareness ('Patient is not enrolled in a clinical trial' matches 'clinical trial'), and 'off-label' classified as experimental when it is a coverage question. Every trigger is a false positive that reaches the right answer by accident. Fixing any of them may stop this case escalating.

DENY-class authored cases drop from 6 to 5. The stratum was already unmeasurable (Wilson about +/-26 pp at n=7, worse now), so this further weakens a measurement that was already not licensing any claim. It strengthens rather than weakens the case for authoring DENY cases.

The 'off-label' reclassification is parked pending a clinician and is the defect most likely to change this case's answer. Off-label use of an FDA-approved drug is a coverage determination under the boundary David set on 2026-07-31; leaving it in the experimental keyword list is a known category error being carried deliberately, not an oversight.

An earlier draft of this change replaced GC-034's reasoning_must_not_include on a false premise -- that 'experimental'/'off-label' were forbidden there and would now conflict. They were not. The replacement would have silently dropped chg-25's F2 morphological backfill ('appropriately', 'appropriateness'). test_gc_034_and_gc_105_appropriately_variant_now_caught went red and caught it. The list is unchanged; the near-miss is recorded because the failure mode -- rewriting a constraint list while changing an outcome -- will recur.

Corpus sensitivity surfaced twice while making this change: the keyword sweep's corpus includes clinical_rationale and judge_scoring_criteria, author-facing prose the model never sees, so editing a case's documentation moves a matcher measurement. Once via the word 'coverage' (pin 152 -> 153) and once via a Python identifier in prose, whose underscore produced a substring hit with no whole-word hit -- manufacturing the exact exposure the sweep exists to measure. Recorded in the test docstring; narrowing the corpus to model-visible fields is its own change.
changes.why_this_component: The defect is in the case, not the detector. Branch 4's OUTCOME on this case is what David wants; only its reasoning is defective. Changing the detector to make GC-034's old DENIED expectation pass would have weakened a safety boundary to accommodate a mis-specified case -- the inverse of the chg-29 error. The detector defects are real and tracked, but they are a separate change with a clinical decision inside it.
changes.rollback_plan: Restore expected_outcome=DENIED, expected_branch=NONE, the previous must_include and judge criteria, and delete the coupling test. The case returns to being permanently unsatisfiable, so the revert restores a known-broken state rather than a working one.

baseline.claim: Before chg-33, GC-034 expected DENIED while its own clinical notes fire the experimental-treatment pre-flight, so the DecisionAgent was never called and the case could not pass.
baseline.verified_by: ClinicalRiskDetector.evaluate() on GC-034; keyword-scan inspection of EXPERIMENTAL_DIAGNOSIS_KEYWORDS against its clinical_notes; two live clinical gate runs.
baseline.result: pre_escalate=True reasons=['experimental_treatment'] deterministically, via five keyword hits ('phase ii', 'clinical trial', 'phase iii', 'phase i', 'off-label') of which all five are false positives. The gate scored GC-034 IN_REVIEW at 0.00 confidence against expected DENIED, judge score 2, on both runs.
